# libreac / fuzz_identity

libreac's own fuzz target `fuzz_identity` ([source](source/fuzz_identity.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libreac 1.9.0 (FreeREAC/libreac at d16f3f4e).

Reads the payload as up to 64 identity-page records (a 16-bit address, biased onto the three modelled ones, and a payload in its own allocation) fed to reac_identity_ingest, each a second time with a guard byte after it, then as the box family, channel widths, capacities and a firmware value with which it calls the firmware and REAC-version formatters, reac_box_name and the catalogue defect check, each output buffer its own allocation of the chosen size.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libreac.a of every src/*.c of libreac 1.9.0 at commit d16f3f4e, compiled with each build's flags, as libreac's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The decode reads no byte past the length it is given (a guard byte after the payload changes nothing), an ignored record changes nothing, and a well-formed firmware, REAC-version or model-name record is never ignored ([lines 180-237](source/fuzz_identity.c#L180-L237)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- An accepted firmware reply is four decimal digits printed as D.DDD, a model name is the payload's text after its first byte, up to its first NUL or the name field's capacity, and never empty, and a REAC-version record keeps its eight bytes, decodes the last three words big-endian and prints as major.minor with a patch of two digits or more; no other address is accepted ([lines 239-332](source/fuzz_identity.c#L239-L332)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each formatter either refuses or writes a NUL-terminated string of the length it returns inside the capacity it was given ([lines 167-175](source/fuzz_identity.c#L167-L175)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The firmware formatter prints any value as its whole part, '.', and three digits, also when the whole part has two digits ([lines 395-411](source/fuzz_identity.c#L395-L411)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The box family is the one the last accepted REAC-version record names in the documented table, and UNKNOWN with no such record or one no row names ([lines 367-374](source/fuzz_identity.c#L367-L374)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- reac_box_name refuses a NULL name buffer or a bad width, and with good widths succeeds exactly when each buffer holds its string; the name is the sent name or family stem plus the two-digit widths, the token is the name lower-cased with its first '-' dropped, the display is "<name> (<in> in / <out> out)", and the catalogue defect mask flags exactly a width or display mismatch ([lines 413-530](source/fuzz_identity.c#L413-L530)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The documented refusals of NULL arguments hold ([lines 341-355](source/fuzz_identity.c#L341-L355)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libreac` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_identity.plain` | 54,112 | `5293a13baa754d43720ab62a9be265d8345cc4845706c3a2f4327b502ffcc070` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_identity.ubsan` | 55,440 | `39abd787960af078dc9d89dfae1bd476448130f16440e97e35aca9c42c80bd48` |
| asan | `fuzz_identity.asan` | 585,464 | `c954b804786cb87fc218414447199e35235b9788453ec0db312f97cd0dc4291b` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_identity.asan-ubsan` | 586,264 | `baf1a4d065e02f55521d39f05d8c8d9ed763a0ef798c70cc3eabe5816ffb3f66` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
